ds is d+1 for M8..M24 (9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25) and d+2 for M30 (32): shank larger than thread (fit bolt) in all rows
k/s between 0.40 and 0.43 and s equals ISO hex AF (13,16,18,21,24,27,30,36,46) for these sizes

shape_hint: Hexagon-head fit (reamer / pass) bolt: a hex head of across-flats s and height k, then a long plain cylindrical fitting shank of diameter ds (ground, one mm larger than the thread) with a shorter reduced thread of diameter d at the end (thread length b, ending in a thread-runout zone between ds and the thread).
notes: DIN 609 (long thread). Sizes in parentheses in the standard ((M14),(M18),(M22),(M27)...) are non-preferred; M14 and M18 are kept (4 / 3 sources). M18 has 3 sources (no German cluster entry). Shank ds is a ground fit diameter (k6) - not equal to the thread. Hex across-flats for M8 is 13 mm (ISO s), M10 16 etc. KS/ISO 7968-type steel construction fit bolts (DIN 7968) are different and were not verified.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched fuller, fasteners.eu, boltport, theo, fastenerdata, wikipedia live (200). Matrix 9 rows (M8-M30) x 6 value columns (P,ds,k,s,b2,b3) x 5 sources: ds,k,s,b2,b3 identical in every source that lists them (fasteners.eu ds/k min-max labels are swapped but nominal rows used; boltport copy typos only in non-kept columns). Clusters: ds 4 (M18: fuller, feu, fd = 3), k 4 (M18 3), s 4 (M18 3), b2/b3 4 (M18 3). P: only fuller prints a coarse-pitch row (fasteners.eu/boltport/theo/fastenerdata tables contain no P row; their M8x1.. rows are fine-pitch) -> 1 cluster, Wikipedia not counted.
problems: P column has a single DIN 609 source (fuller); the 'kova DIN 933/6914' and Wikipedia cross-checks are other parts / not distributor pages -> drop P
Table is DIN 609 (LONG thread) only; family label 'DIN 609 · DIN 610 · DIN 7968': DIN 610 has shorter thread b (e.g. M8 13.5/18.5), DIN 7968 is a different part - do not present as covering them
M14 and M18 are non-preferred sizes ('(M14)','(M18)' in fuller, fasteners.eu, boltport); M18 has exactly 3 clusters (no German row)
ds is a k6 fit-shank NOMINAL (fuller 'Nominal Size (K6)'); tolerance limits not published
